comment_text.value:
I am attempting this with a 100 MB GameMaker (HoloCure) game to make mobile and console ports for fun. Because it uses YYC[0] instead of running in a VM which is how GameMaker games usually work (to my crude understanding of the issue) I have to reverse engineer it instead of just extracting assets and putting them into a project template.

I am using Qwen 3.8 27B-8bit in oMLX and Pi agent with GhidraMCP on my MacBook M3 Max. So far it ran for like 10 hours total and I haven't checked in on it much but it seems to have extracted the audio assets successfully and wrote a whole bunch of helper scripts for Ghidra to extract YYC functions which took several hours to run. I put the project on hold cause I didn't want to keep running it at 100% fans for hours every day. It blew through ~200k context of the model 3 times by now. I am not confident in this project, especially because I have very little experience doing grown up reverse engineering that isn't decompiling a C# or Android apps so I can't really guide it.

0 - https://manual.gamemaker.io/lts/en/Settings/YoYo_Compiler.ht...

> the LLM tells are impossible to ignore. Bluntly, your intellectual fly is open: lots of people notice — but no one is pointing it out

You are going to be left in the dust with this attitude.

People using LLMs will continue to school you; not just because of your disrespectful attitude.

To assume that people have not read what they've used an AI to generate is to make a number of mistakes.

1. People using (assistive) LLMs needn't cow to you due to your aesthetic rejection of LLM-generated text. It is impolite for you to assert your superiority to make them feel inferior.

2. Your aesthetic reaction to their prose is not a sufficient estimator of sufficiency.

3. These generations of LLMs are already superhuman in so many dimensions. If you focus on the color of the paint - here, the wording of their reply increase of the substance of their argument - you will have wasted their and your own time.

It sounds like you are frustrated that LLMs are besting you in your field and you've chosen to trash talk on your blog to solve the problem.

Should people reversing with e.g. GhidraMCP stop and focus on the LLM-generated aesthetics of a watermarked prosaic vulnerability assessment?

comment_text.value:
Author here. Great question — the MCP landscape for Ghidra has exploded lately. Here's my take:

*LaurieWired's GhidraMCP* (the one I contribute to): Most complete toolset — 110+ MCP tools, 130+ REST endpoints. Active development, Ghidra 11.3-12.0.2 support, localhost-only binding for security. Best for interactive RE sessions with Claude/GPT where you want maximum capability.

*pyghidra-mcp*: Runs headless via pyghidra. Great for batch processing or CI pipelines, but you lose the GUI workflow.

*ReVa*: More of an autonomous agent approach — it tries to do RE for you rather than with you. Different philosophy, interesting for automated triage.

*GhidrAssist*: Focuses on the Ghidra plugin side, less on MCP integration.

If you want the most tools and active maintenance for interactive AI-assisted RE, LaurieWired's is what I'd recommend. I've been using it for multi-version game RE (Diablo 2, GTA) and it handles the "analyze v1.07, port annotations to v1.08" workflow really well.

story_title.value: Show HN: Ghidra MCP Server – 110 tools for AI-assisted reverse engineering
